targets.approach: Roadside Cave is a south-facing limestone cliff just west of Trail Lake Road (County Road 411), above the inlet to Trail Lake. The route is on the far left wall, left of the main wall.
targets.descent_text: After topping out, walk off to either side.
targets.name: Indian cave.

targets.approach: Leave the vehicle in the lot and take the trail beside the river down to a big rock; the outcrop of rock slabs is on the far side of the river, which means fording the river and then walking up to them.
targets.name: 2 beers and a joint.

targets.approach: Leave the vehicle in the lot and take the trail beside the river down to a big rock; the slabs are on the far side of the river, so you have to cross it and walk up. The top of the slab can be reached by walking around, which gives access to build a top-rope anchor from rocks.

Springfield Gully is a short walk from the camp in the Cirque of the Towers, in the cuts of the buttress at the edge of camp, below the Watchtower. A climbers' path from the campsites runs under the gentle slabs on both sides; most of the routes here lie in the left-hand cut. Walk up the gully to a hidden wall on the south side, where Kamp Krusty is the largest continuous crack.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the gear anchor to climber's left, down the narrow gap beside the crack.
targets.name: Kamp Krusty

targets.approach: Springfield Gully is a short walk from the camp in the Cirque of the Towers, in the cuts of the buttress at the edge of camp, below the Watchtower. Follow the gully's north side upward beyond a long slabby block; the route is on a small west-facing in-cut on the northern edge of the gully.
targets.descent_text: Downclimb the short chimney when done.
targets.name: Spiderpig

targets.approach: St. Lawrence Basin is a remote group of cirques approached from the east, above the valley floor near Dubois. The route climbs the evident arete on Lightning Rod Spire.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route; all the anchors are bolted.
targets.name: Ride The Lightning

targets.approach: St. Lawrence Basin is a remote group of cirques approached from the east, above the valley floor near Dubois. The route climbs a prominent spur jutting out from the west end of Saddle Mountain's north face.
targets.name: Saddle  Mountain North Buttress

targets.approach: Follow the Dry Horse Creek trail up to a point even with the tower, then go up the mahogany-covered hillside to the tower's west end. The route starts in the dihedral just left of the west arete and finishes on the east arete.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the southwest face to the ground.
targets.name: Ragtime Cowboy Joe

targets.approach: Sunrise Ridge continues Taminah Arete: from the top of Taminah Arete, descend with a rappel and a downclimb to the saddle on the north between Matternaught and Gilkey, then begin from the saddle's west side. Taminah Arete itself is reached by heading northwest from the lake's west end, going beneath the East Ridge buttress, and finding a weakness at the west end of the cliff band guarding its base.
targets.descent_text: The route finishes on the summit of Gilkey Tower. Descend Garnet Canyon by the South Teton trail.
targets.name: Sunrise Ridge

targets.approach: The Old Log Dam is the first wall in Warm Spring Canyon: take the trail from the parking lot beside the creek. The route is at the end of the main wall.
targets.name: Hippie

targets.approach: The Cirque of the Towers is entered from the Big Sandy trailhead, following a long trail into the cirque. Scramble up talus and ledges on the far left side of Warrior I, avoiding the slabs directly below the route, then cut back right to the routes when you reach the main upper ledge systems. The route starts on the ledge where the Northeast Face line cuts off to the right, and runs up left-trending ledges to the foot of the evident corner system under a roof.
targets.descent_text: Cross the top of the tower to the rappel route that goes down the Northeast Face.
targets.name: East Face, Left

targets.approach: The Cirque of the Towers is entered from the Big Sandy trailhead, following a long trail into the cirque. Enter the Warrior I basin, a bit north (left) of the peak, and scramble the grassy ledges rightward until the ground cliffs out; the route starts there, following a ramp system angling up and right.
targets.descent_text: Rappel down climber's left of the route.
targets.name: Northeast Face R of Warrior I

targets.approach: From the Caves camp, take the main trail toward the Lower Saddle, cross the creek that drains the Teepe Glacier, and take the trail toward the glacier and the guide-service camp. Walk part of the way up toward the glacier, ford the creek a second time and hop boulders to the foot of the tower, which is on your right. The route is on the left of the line called Good over Evil, keeping to the ridge.
targets.descent_text: The tower can be descended by rappelling off the top on the side facing the meadows.
targets.name: The Pretender
targets.parent: Garnet Canyon Rock Climbs-Not Disappointment Peak

targets.approach: Drive Highway 16 west from Buffalo, turn right at the Hunter Creek Trailhead sign, take the left fork onto Forest Service Road 391 (rocky; high clearance is recommended) and park at the Enormodome camp, just right of the road at the edge of a large meadow. A faint path leads north from camp to a cattle trail heading northeast; leave it to skirt the boggy meadow on its north side, and a cleared path through the young forest runs straight to the south prow of the dome. The West Face is on the west flank of the fin, and an access staircase in the middle of it gives a third-class scramble to the top. The route is near the centre of the face, left of the staircase.
targets.descent_text: Lower off the clip-and-lower anchors at the top.
targets.name: Sold it Out
